title: Examples: add batching_tier to requests + validation via response headers and metrics
author: Alex Martinez
description:
## Summary This updates the example apps to (a) set `batching_tier` explicitly and (b) show users how to validate the tier is actually in effect using response headers and standard Redwood metrics. This is meant to reduce "I set cost-efficient but nothing changed" support loops and to make the tier feature discoverable as it rolls into beta. The examples intentionally avoid any new API surface; they only use request fields that are already accepted by the platform and then read back the effective config from headers/telemetry.

## Context / why Now that tiered batching defaults are landing behind a flag in runtime, we need examples that demonstrate: 1) how to choose a tier per route (chat/completions vs embeddings), and 2) how to confirm you’re getting the intended scheduler behavior (queue delay / batch formation) without guessing based on latency alone.

Related: ENG-18426 (SDK snippets), PM-412 (launch plan). This PR is aligned with the Console work to expose effective defaults, but the examples here rely only on response headers + metrics that are already available in the hosted stack.

## What changed - Adds a `BATCHING_TIER` env var (default: `standard`) across example apps and wires it into requests as `batching_tier: fast|standard|cost_efficient`. - Adds a small "Validate batching tier" section to each README: shows which response headers to look for and which metrics/dashboards to use to confirm behavior. - Adds an opt-in debug mode (`REDWOOD_DEBUG_EFFECTIVE_CONFIG=1`) that prints relevant headers and a short interpretation (e.g., max_queue_delay_ms and max_batch tokens) to stdout.

## Validation approach in examples ### Response headers (immediate, per-request) Examples now log these when `REDWOOD_DEBUG_EFFECTIVE_CONFIG=1`: - `x-redwood-batching-tier`: the tier the scheduler resolved to (after any policy override) - `x-redwood-effective-max-queue-delay-ms`: effective queue delay cap used for batch formation - `x-redwood-effective-max-batch-tokens`: effective max batch tokens (if applicable) - `x-redwood-request-route`: route used (chat/completions/embeddings) These are meant to be used as a sanity check while tuning. If any of these headers are missing, the README calls out common causes (older region, feature flag off, gateway not configured to pass through headers).

### Metrics (behavior over time) Each README also points to the metrics that correlate with the tier behavior: - `redwood_inference_queue_delay_ms` (p50/p95/p99) - `redwood_inference_batch_size` distribution - `redwood_inference_batch_wait_ms` distribution - `redwood_inference_tokens_per_sec` + GPU util (where available) The examples include a short note that latency alone is insufficient (workload mix changes can swamp the signal), and that queue delay + batch size distribution should move in the expected direction when switching tiers.

## Changed areas/files - `chat-node/` (TS): add `batching_tier` to request payload; add header logging helper - `chat-python/`: same; plus README section on tier selection and validation - `embeddings-batch/`: defaults to `cost_efficient` (since it’s non-streaming) and explains why - `shared/headers.ts` + `shared/headers.py`: utilities to parse/print effective-config headers - README updates across the above

## Illustrative snippet (TS) ```ts const batchingTier = (process.env.BATCHING_TIER ?? "standard") as "fast" | "standard" | "cost_efficient"; const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: process.env.REDWOOD_MODEL ?? "rw-llama-3-70b-instruct", messages, stream: true, batching_tier: batchingTier, }); if (process.env.REDWOOD_DEBUG_EFFECTIVE_CONFIG === "1") { logEffectiveBatching(resp.response.headers); } ```

## Notes / caveats - Streaming: README notes that `fast` is recommended for interactive streaming routes (token cadence sensitivity) and calls out that `cost_efficient` may increase time-to-first-token due to queueing. - Overrides: README includes a short explanation that explicit batching knobs (if set) take precedence over tier defaults; for examples we intentionally do NOT set manual knobs to keep behavior attributable to tiers. - Header propagation: For some environments (older private installs / proxies), response headers can be stripped. The validation section includes a fallback: use metrics/traces.

## Test plan - `pnpm test` in `chat-node/` - `pytest` in `chat-python/` - Manual smoke: run `chat-node` against staging with `BATCHING_TIER=fast` and verify `x-redwood-batching-tier=fast` appears; repeat with `cost_efficient` and observe queue delay distribution shift in dashboard.

## Screenshots Not included (CLI output only). Example log output is in the READMEs.

## Checklist - [x] No breaking changes - [x] Examples still run with older SDKs (tier is optional) - [x] Tier names match runtime (`cost_efficient`, not `eco`) - [x] Added troubleshooting notes for missing headers

## Rollout / impact None. Repo is examples-only; used by docs and Solutions Engineering. Once merged, we can link these from the beta release notes and Optimize docs.
commits: examples(shared): add effective-config header parsing utilities
examples(chat-node): wire batching_tier env var into streaming chat request
examples(chat-python): add batching_tier + debug logging + README validation section
examples(embeddings-batch): default to cost_efficient tier + metrics validation notes
docs(readmes): troubleshooting section for missing headers/metrics
review_conversation:
Monica Patel (review): Tier enum naming: please use `cost_efficient` exactly (matches SDK typing + runtime schema). Also can we avoid printing headers by default? Alex Martinez (author): Updated to `cost_efficient` everywhere and gated header printing behind `REDWOOD_DEBUG_EFFECTIVE_CONFIG=1`.

Nikhil Sharma (review): For streaming chat, can we default to `standard` rather than `fast`? We don’t want to implicitly recommend a tier that might be capacity constrained during beta. Alex Martinez (author): Kept default as `standard` and added note: use `fast` for interactive streaming SLOs; link to docs section.

Chloe Martin (review): The metric names—are they final? We’ve had churn here historically. Alex Martinez (author): Used the names from current observability pack. Added a note that dashboards may alias the metrics and that queue-delay histogram is the stable signal.

Monica Patel (follow-up): Can you add a troubleshooting bullet for proxies stripping headers? Alex Martinez (author): Added under "If headers are missing" with a metrics-only fallback.

Approvals: Monica Patel approved; Nikhil Sharma approved; Chloe Martin approved.
release_notes: Examples now show how to set `batching_tier` (fast/standard/cost_efficient).
Examples document how to validate tier behavior via response headers and queue-delay/batch metrics.
